# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 41 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 41 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_041_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 10 — Put Away Grief

**41:1** "Put away grief from yourself," he said, "for she is the sister of double-mindedness and of bitterness." "How, lord," I asked, "is she the sister of these? For bitterness and double-mindedness seem to me to be different things." "You are senseless, O man," he said. "Do you not perceive that grief is the most evil of all the spirits, the most pernicious for the servants of God, destroying a man beyond all the other spirits, and wearing out the Holy Spirit, while also saving it?"

**41:2** "I am without understanding, lord," I said, "and cannot grasp these comparisons. For how it can wear out and also save I cannot comprehend." "Hear then," he said. "Those who have never sought the truth or inquired concerning God, but have simply believed — and have become entangled in business pursuits and wealth and friendships with the Gentiles and many other concerns of this age — those who are preoccupied with such things have no grasp of the comparisons of the divine. For they are darkened by these occupations and corrupted and rendered barren."

**41:3** "But those who fear God and inquire concerning the divine and truth, and direct their hearts toward the Lord — to them all things are readily grasped, and they understand everything that is said to them, because the fear of the Lord is in them. For where the Lord dwells, there is great understanding. Cleave therefore to the Lord, and you will understand and comprehend all things."

**41:4** "Hear now, O senseless one, how grief wears out the Holy Spirit and how it saves it. When the double-minded man undertakes any work and fails at it on account of his double-mindedness, grief enters the man and grieves the Holy Spirit and wears it out."

**41:5** "Again, when bitterness cleaves to a man and he is embittered over some matter — whether a transaction, or food, or some foolish word that was spoken, or a friend, or a giving or receiving, or some other such foolish things — grief enters into the heart of the man who has been embittered, and he is disturbed and the Holy Spirit is grieved."

**41:6** "Again, anger when it comes upon a man and he is made bitter on account of some matter — and once more on account of these same things grief enters and makes the heart of the man sad. Thus it wears out the Holy Spirit. But hear now in what way it saves: when a sinner recognizes his transgressions and repents, grief comes upon him as his salvation. Now this grief over sins is saving. Both griefs are found in concert: the grief that saves and the grief that destroys."

**41:7** "Therefore clothe yourself with cheerfulness, which always has favor before God and is pleasing to him, and rejoice in it. For every cheerful person does good deeds and thinks good thoughts and despises grief. But the sorrowful person always does evil — first, because he grieves the Holy Spirit, which was given to man as a gift of joy; and second, because in grieving the Holy Spirit he works lawlessness, praying to God neither in due form nor rendering thanks to him. Therefore the prayer of a sorrowful person has no power to mount up to the altar of God."

**41:8** "Why is that?" I asked. "Because grief sits in his heart," he said. "Grief mingled with prayer does not permit the prayer to ascend in purity to the altar. For as wine blended with vinegar no longer retains the same pleasant taste, so also grief blended with the Holy Spirit does not have the same intercession. Therefore cleanse yourself from this evil grief, and you shall live to God; and all who cast grief from themselves and clothe themselves with all cheerfulness shall live to God."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and ethical-pneumatological precision.*
